content:
At the beginning of June, we had already pointed out three cases of sanctioned Russian banks bypassing review and getting their client applications listed on the App Store. Two months later, new examples have emerged again, and one of them shot straight to the top of the iPhone App Store download charts upon its debut.

The latest case is K8CHEN PRO. On the App Store, it is packaged as an application that uses augmented reality (AR) features to help you design your kitchen.

However, the moment you open the app, the disguise falls apart immediately. The privacy policy linked on the App Store was apparently generated by "Free Privacy Policy Generator"—that alone is already suspicious enough.

In short, this app is definitely T-Bank's client application. What puzzles me most is how these kinds of apps can keep passing the App Store's review mechanisms.

When they climb the App Store charts due to the attention they attract, anyone can see at a glance that these apps simply should not be there. The situation is really quite intriguing.

The two cases from June can be revisited here and here respectively.

Update: Sure enough, this app has already been taken down from the App Store.
